rationale: Read the retained receipt of experiment d2f4dd956a5f4fd58153c64951b930f0-experiment (CheckRun 666f0626e67340a491ab414403fd1e6b, exit 0, 30 events). The setup event 28 records the node's recovered set as three voters while the configuration in force lists five, and the result event 29 records the vote from the candidate outside the recovered set being refused while the control candidate inside it was granted, with both candidates being members of the configuration in force. The question is therefore a witnessed violation, and a behavior entry records it.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with the smaller configuration recorded in its snapshot refuses a vote request from a server that the configuration in force lists as a voter but its recovered voter set does not contain, while the same request shape from a candidate inside the recovered set is granted; because both requests carried the leadership-transfer flag, the difference is attributable to the membership rule alone.
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a commit-tracking store; the node restarts from a snapshot recording a three-voter configuration while the configuration in force has five voters and the recommitting entry is in its log but outside the restart scan; the outside candidate is a voter in the configuration in force.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: the same recovered configuration that lets a stale node admit ineligible peers on some paths also makes it refuse eligible ones on the vote path. Parsed event 28 records the premise: the node's recovered configuration holds three voters while the configuration in force lists five, and both candidates used in the comparison are members of the configuration in force. Parsed event 29 records the outcome: the vote from the candidate outside the recovered set was not granted, the vote from the candidate inside it was granted, and the derived predicate that the stale set does not reject a member of the configuration in force is violated. The comparison isolates the membership rule because both requests were identical in term, log recency and the leadership-transfer flag, so the leader-availability rejection could not decide either, and the only difference was the candidate identity. Mechanism from source: requestVote rejects a candidate that its own Servers list does not contain, and that list is the configuration the node recovered; the restart path leaves that configuration behind the log's committed history, so a voter added after the node's snapshot is unknown to it. Consequence: a candidate that needs that node's vote to assemble a majority of the configuration in force may fail to be elected even though the node is counted as a voter by everyone else, which is a bounded liveness effect on how support is formed rather than a change in what may be committed. The effect is bounded by the repair path, since any later configuration entry or installed snapshot restores the full set.
counterevidence: The rejected candidate can still be elected if it gathers a majority without this node, so the effect only removes one possible supporter rather than making elections impossible in general.

The node itself is still counted as a voter by the other members, so a cluster that has lost exactly one other voter can be left without a reachable majority while this node refuses to help form one, which is why the consequence is bounded rather than global.
Any later configuration entry or installed snapshot repairs the recovered set, and the probe deliberately keeps the configuration stable and the node isolated from the repair.
The two requests were delivered through the in-memory transport with a candidate identity supplied by the probe rather than produced by a real election.
limitations: Measured on one five-peer in-memory cluster with the repository's own facilities; production transports and timing are not covered.
The probe exercises the vote handler directly at the transport boundary, so the effect on a full election campaign is argued from that handler rather than measured end to end.
The stale set here is the snapshot's three-voter configuration; other stale shapes (for example a removed voter still present) are not measured.
